core.title: Reference only registered contracts as flow router message payloads
core.given: A flow router artifact has messages that reference payload contract identities.
core.when: The plan reaches the CONFIRM phase; every referenced payload contract identity is checked, whether or not the reference changed.
core.then: Every payload contract identity referenced by a flow router message must resolve to an authored entry in the contracts registry, not merely to a contract file that exists or matches by name.
prefer: Look up the identity in the contracts registry, the single source of truth mapping identity to path, theme, producers and consumers, and reference an identity that is a member of it.
If the needed contract is not yet registered, plan its authoring and registration as part of the work before referencing it.
When a registry entry is removed or renamed, update the flow router messages that reference it.
avoid: Pointing the payload at a contract file that merely exists or matches by name without an entry in the contracts registry.
Inventing a contract identity in the flow router that no registry entry backs.
core.why: The contracts registry is the single source of truth for identity -> path -> theme -> producers -> consumers; a file that merely matches by name is not sufficient to count as a registered contract.
evidence: The registry-resolution check for flow router payload contracts passes at CONFIRM.
On failure, the report names the flow router, the message, the referenced contract identity, and the registry.
verification: A reference-resolution check over every payload contract identity referenced by a flow router message in the plan, including unchanged references (registry edits and removals can invalidate unchanged references).
Resolution means membership in the authored contracts registry; a contract file that merely exists or matches by name on the filesystem does not count as resolution.
Enforced at phase CONFIRM and confirm-blocking: a failure blocks the plan at CONFIRM.
On failure, the finding names the flow router, the message, the referenced contract identity, and the registry (its path).
The concrete detector/validator and its validation-family, template and variant identifiers are realization details named in the stack sidecar, not in the core.

fires: At CONFIRM, a flow router message's payload names a contract identity that is not an entry in the contracts registry, even though a contract file matching that name exists on disk.
At CONFIRM, an unchanged flow router message references a payload contract identity whose registry entry was removed or renamed.
At CONFIRM, a plan in which a planner authored or edited a flow router message payload contract identity to a value absent from the contracts registry.
doesNotFire: Every payload contract identity referenced by flow router messages is an entry in the contracts registry.
Planning artifacts with no flow router messages (e.g. plain product capability or acceptance docs that declare no flow router payloads).
Before CONFIRM (e.g. while a plan is still being drafted); the check is enforced at CONFIRM.

profileRequirements.meaning: Where the authored contracts registry lives: the single index mapping a payload contract identity to its artifact path, theme, producers and consumers; membership in it is what counts as a registered contract.

neutralityNotes: Method terms kept as-is because they belong to the ATDD method, not to a stack: flow router (plan artifact kind), payload contract identity, contracts registry, and the phase name CONFIRM (also used as an activation fact value). The core names no stack, runtime, tool, file suffix or path; the only concrete datum it needs, the registry's location, arrives via the proposed profile key layout.registries#contracts (the closed vocabulary has no key for it). The validator id and the validation family/template/variant identifiers are realization details and remain bunOnly; severity 3 and disposition strict are carried in core:verification per notProfileKeys. No exception was dropped or added: bun.json declares no 'unless' entries, and the additions (prefer[1], prefer[2], activation scenarios) are restated neutrally without changing the obligation.
